chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Khunays, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sayābah has a debt owed to him by a man who has died, and we spoke to him to absolve it, but he refused.
He عليه السلام said: Woe to him! Does he not know that for him there are ten for every dirham if he absolves it? But if he does not absolve it, then he only has a dirham in exchange for a dirham.

key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a dirham; here, a unit of debt and reward comparison
key_terms.عَشَرَةً: tenfold reward in return for remission of the debt
key_terms.وَيْحَهُ: an expression of reproach and pity, meaning 'woe to him'
key_terms.يُحَلِّلَهُ: to absolve or release the debtor from the claim

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for forgiving the debt of a deceased debtor in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the merit of forgiving a debt owed by a deceased person. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام emphasizes that remitting such a debt brings multiplied divine reward, whereas insisting on repayment yields only its equivalent. The report highlights both financial ethics and concern for one’s reward in the Hereafter.
